name: Amey
desc: British infrastructure support services provider maintaining roads, rail, utilities and public-sector facilities across the UK.
ownership: private equity: Buckthorn Partners and One Equity Partners
capacity_detail: Revenue GBP 1.9bn in 2024 (approx. USD 2.5bn at GBP 1.30)
markets: UK infrastructure services for road, rail, utilities, defence and public-sector clients across England, Scotland and Wales
rationale: Large UK contractor could use F1 hospitality at Silverstone to entertain government and utility clients and support graduate engineering recruitment.

name: Perenco
desc: Independent Anglo-French oil and gas exploration and production company operating mature fields across Africa, Latin America and Asia.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 7bn in 2021 (approx. USD 7.7bn at EUR 1.10); owned by the Perrodo family
markets: Oil and gas production in Africa (Cameroon, Gabon, Congo, Tunisia), Latin America, Trinidad, Vietnam and the UK North Sea
rationale: Family-owned energy producer with deep pockets; F1 hospitality could support relationships with host governments, though low consumer brand need.

name: Canonical
desc: London-based software company behind the Ubuntu Linux operating system, selling enterprise support, security and cloud services.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 344.5m in 2025 (filed annual report and accounts)
markets: Enterprise Linux, cloud and IoT software sold worldwide, with offices in London, Austin, Boston, Shanghai, Taipei and Tokyo
rationale: Ubuntu runs on cloud and edge infrastructure; F1 team technology partnerships offer a showcase alongside rival enterprise software sponsors.

name: Dura Vermeer
desc: Dutch construction group building homes, offices, roads, railways and pipelines through building, infrastructure and technical divisions.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.1bn in 2024 (approx. USD 2.3bn at EUR 1.10)
markets: Mainly the Netherlands: housing, utility building, roads, rail and technical installations
rationale: Dutch F1 enthusiasm around the Zandvoort Grand Prix makes F1 hospitality useful for client relationships and recruiting engineers.

name: Haskoning
desc: Independent Dutch engineering and consultancy firm advising on water, infrastructure, buildings, industry and energy projects worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 698.8m in 2022 (approx. USD 769m at EUR 1.10); described as not stock-market listed
markets: Consulting and engineering via about 70 offices; home markets include Netherlands, UK, Canada, India, Indonesia, Poland, South Africa, US
rationale: Engineering consultancy rebranded in 2025; F1 technical association could support its new brand and talent recruitment internationally.

name: Jumbo Supermarkten
desc: Second-largest Dutch supermarket chain with over 700 stores, owned by the Van Eerd family through Jumbo Food Groep.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 10.89bn in 2023 (approx. USD 12bn at EUR 1.10)
markets: Supermarkets and online grocery in the Netherlands and Belgium, about 20% Dutch market share
rationale: Consumer brand in a country with huge F1 following around Zandvoort and Verstappen; F1 could drive in-store promotions and loyalty.

name: Lely
desc: Dutch maker of milking robots, feeding robots and data systems for dairy farms, with plants in Maassluis and Pella.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1,014m in 2025 (approx. USD 1.1bn at EUR 1.10)
markets: Dairy robotics sold in more than forty countries; production in the Netherlands and the United States
rationale: Robotics engineering brand could use an F1 technical partnership to signal innovation to farmers and attract engineering talent.

name: Ayesa
desc: Seville-based engineering and technology services group working on metros, infrastructure, chemical engineering and digital projects.
ownership: private equity: A&M Capital Europe (shareholder since 2021)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 800m in 2025 (approx. USD 880m at EUR 1.10)
markets: Engineering and IT services in Spain, Latin America, Asia including Japan, and metro projects worldwide
rationale: Growing via acquisitions with PE backing; F1 B2B hospitality could support its push into technology services for international clients.

name: Iberostar
desc: Mallorca-based hotel group owned by the Fluxá family, operating beach and urban resorts in Europe and the Americas.
capacity_detail: Managed revenue EUR 5.1bn in 2025 (approx. USD 5.6bn at EUR 1.10); revenue EUR 4,468m in 2024
markets: Hotels and resorts in Spain, Mediterranean, Caribbean, Mexico and Latin America
rationale: Premium leisure brand targeting European and American travellers; F1 race weekends in Spain, Miami and Mexico match its markets.

name: Eurostars Hotel Company (Grupo Hotusa)
desc: Barcelona-based tourism group behind Eurostars Hotel Company and the Hotusa independent hotel network, founded in 1977.
capacity_detail: Global turnover of hotel management and tourism services above EUR 1.2bn in 2019 (approx. USD 1.3bn at EUR 1.10)
markets: Hotel management and tourism services in Spain, Europe and the Americas
rationale: Urban hotel brand with Spanish and European reach could host F1 travel packages around Barcelona and other European Grands Prix.

name: IDOM
desc: Employee-owned Spanish engineering, consulting and architecture firm working on infrastructure, industry and energy projects worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 350m in 2016 (approx. USD 385m at EUR 1.10)
markets: Engineering and architecture projects in Spain and worldwide, about 3,500 staff
rationale: Engineering firm with industrial and energy clients; F1 hospitality and technical association could help recruitment and client entertainment.

name: Cosentino
desc: Family-owned Spanish manufacturer of engineered stone surfaces such as Silestone and Dekton, selling mainly abroad.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1,570m in 2023 (approx. USD 1.7bn at EUR 1.10); 92% from international markets
sponsorships: Collaborates with the Mutua Madrid Open tennis tournament; sponsors Peneque Pro sailing team at Copa del Rey Mapfre
markets: Surfaces for kitchens and architecture sold worldwide, 92% of sales outside Spain, major markets in US and Europe
rationale: Design-led consumer brand already active in sports sponsorship; F1's premium global audience suits Silestone and Dekton positioning.

name: Werfen
desc: Family-owned Barcelona company making specialized diagnostics for hemostasis, acute care, transfusion, autoimmunity and transplant testing.
capacity_detail: Worldwide sales of almost EUR 2.2bn in 2024 (approx. USD 2.4bn at EUR 1.10)
markets: Operates directly in 30 countries and in over 100 territories through distributors; technology centres in US and Europe
rationale: Hospital-facing B2B diagnostics brand; F1 offers limited consumer value, but hospitality could serve global distributor and customer relations.

name: Mecalux
desc: Barcelona-based maker of warehouse racking, automated storage, robotics and warehouse management software, controlled by the Carrillo family.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1,147m stated in infobox (approx. USD 1.26bn at EUR 1.10); article cites audited 2025 figures, year not explicit
markets: Own sales network in 24 countries and 12 production centres across Europe, North America and South America

signals.ipo: Preparing stock-market listing for April, reported by Cinco Días (Nov 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mecalux)

rationale: Logistics automation leader whose clients include F1 sponsors' sectors; F1 logistics showcase fits ahead of a planned stock-market debut.

name: Archirodon Group
desc: Dutch-Greek contractor building and maintaining ports, marine infrastructure, pipelines and other major construction projects.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1bn in 2021 (approx. USD 1.1bn at EUR 1.10)
markets: Marine and infrastructure construction with major presence in Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt and Greece
rationale: Gulf-focused contractor; F1 races in Saudi Arabia, Abu Dhabi and Qatar could serve client hospitality with regional governments.

name: Empik Group
desc: Polish omnichannel retailer of books, music, media and leisure products, with 386 stores, e-commerce and marketplace.
capacity_detail: Revenue PLN 3.44bn in 2025 (approx. USD 930m at PLN 0.27)
markets: Poland: 386 stores, online shop, marketplace, Empik Go audiobooks app, 12 million customers
rationale: Consumer retail brand reaching 12 million Poles; F1 content and promotions could build engagement, though reach is domestic.

name: RTB House
desc: Polish advertising technology company using deep learning for retargeting and programmatic ad campaigns in over 70 markets.
ownership: private equity: Cinven (stake bought from founders)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 408.59m in 2022 (approx. USD 449m at EUR 1.10)
markets: Ad campaigns in over 70 markets; 90% of revenue earned outside Poland
rationale: Global B2B ad-tech brand; F1 digital audiences and marketer hospitality fit its pitch to brand and agency clients.

name: Lantmännen
desc: Swedish agricultural cooperative owned by 19,000 farmers, active in farming inputs, machinery, energy and food brands.
capacity_detail: Annual turnover about SEK 18bn in 2024 per article infobox (approx. USD 1.7bn at SEK 0.095)
markets: Operations in over 20 countries, mainly Sweden and Northern Europe, 10,000 employees
rationale: Nordic food and farm co-op with consumer bakery brands; F1 has limited fit, but could support brand-building in Northern Europe.

name: CSS Insurance
desc: Swiss health, accident and property insurer covering about 1.7 million people through around 100 agencies.
ownership: association-owned: CSS Association (sole shareholder; not stock-exchange listed)
capacity_detail: Premium volume about CHF 7.8bn (approx. USD 9.8bn at CHF 1.25), current company page
markets: Switzerland only: health, accident and property insurance for about 1.7 million people
rationale: Domestic Swiss insurer; F1 reach far exceeds its market, so fit is weak beyond Swiss hospitality.

name: Edmond de Rothschild
desc: Family-owned Geneva banking group offering private banking, asset management and private equity, delisted from Zurich in 2019.
capacity_detail: Revenue CHF 6.3bn in 2024 per Wikipedia infobox (approx. USD 7.9bn at CHF 1.25); figure looks high for the group
markets: Private banking and asset management from Geneva, Paris, Luxembourg, Monaco and other centres; lifestyle brands in wine and hotels
rationale: Wealth-management brand targeting rich clients; F1 Paddock Club hospitality and Monaco fit its client base, like rival UBS.

name: Hero Group
industry: fruit spreads and baby food maker
desc: Swiss food group making fruit spreads, baby food and cereal bars, owned by the Oetker family since 2003.
capacity_detail: Revenue CHF 1.2bn in 2023 (approx. USD 1.5bn at CHF 1.25)
markets: Food brands sold in Europe, the US and other markets worldwide
rationale: Branded consumer foods group; F1 could support international brand awareness, though its family-focused products fit F1 less well.

name: Manor
desc: Switzerland's largest department-store chain, headquartered in Basel and owned by Maus Frères of Geneva.
capacity_detail: Total sales CHF 3bn in 2013 (approx. USD 3.75bn at CHF 1.25)
markets: Department stores across Switzerland
rationale: Domestic Swiss retailer; F1 global scale is a poor match beyond Swiss customer promotions.

name: Pictet Group
desc: Geneva private bank and asset manager owned by its managing partners, with over CHF 800 billion under management.
capacity_detail: Operating income CHF 3.2bn in 2025 (approx. USD 4bn at CHF 1.25), Group annual report
markets: Wealth and asset management from offices in Europe, Asia, North America and the Middle East
rationale: Swiss wealth manager whose rival UBS sponsors F1; Paddock Club hospitality reaches the same high-net-worth clients globally.

name: Swissport
desc: Swiss provider of airport ground services and air cargo handling, serving about 243 million passengers in 2025.
ownership: private equity: investor group led by Strategic Value Partners, Apollo, TowerBrook and Ares funds
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.99bn in 2018 (approx. USD 3.3bn at EUR 1.10)
markets: Ground handling and cargo at airports in Europe, Americas, Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa
rationale: Global aviation services brand; F1's own air-freight logistics give a credible story, though its customers are airlines not consumers.

name: Eti
desc: Turkish maker of biscuits, wafers, chocolate and breakfast foods, founded in 1962 by Firuz Kanatlı.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.3bn in 2023
sponsorships: Main sponsor of Eskişehirspor football club
markets: Snacks sold across Turkey and exported; acquired Vancouver-based plant-based snack firm Trubar in November 2025

signals.regions: Acquired Vancouver-based Trubar for about USD 142m (Nov 2025; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eti_(company))

rationale: Expanding snack brand entering North America; F1's young global audience could support its push beyond Turkey.

name: LC Waikiki
desc: Turkish value fashion retailer with over 1,200 stores, owned by the Küçük, Dizdar, Kısacık and Amouyal families.
capacity_detail: Net sales about USD 4.92bn in 2024
markets: Over 1,200 stores in Turkey, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Central Asia; online sales
rationale: Mass-market fashion retailer expanding abroad; F1 races in its Middle East and European markets could raise brand profile.

name: Sütaş Group
desc: Turkish dairy company producing milk, yoghurt, cheese and ayran, employing around 5,000 people.
capacity_detail: Revenue TRY 28.69bn in 2023 (approx. USD 690m at current TRY 0.024)
markets: Dairy products in Turkey and neighbouring countries
rationale: Domestic-focused dairy brand; F1 offers limited fit unless it pursues international expansion.

name: Raben Group
desc: Family-run Dutch logistics group providing contract logistics, warehousing, road distribution and sea and air freight in Europe.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.5bn in 2021 (approx. USD 1.65bn at EUR 1.10)
markets: Logistics across Central and Eastern Europe, Germany, the Netherlands and Italy
rationale: European logistics group; F1 hospitality could support client relations, as rival DHL already sponsors F1.

name: Kramp
desc: Dutch family business distributing spare parts and accessories for agriculture, forestry and outdoor machinery across Europe.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1,253m in 2025 (approx. USD 1.38bn at EUR 1.10)
markets: Parts distribution to dealers and farmers across Europe
rationale: B2B parts distributor; F1 has little relevance to its dealer customers beyond hospitality.

name: Strawberry
desc: Nordic hotel group with about 250 hotels, owned by Petter Stordalen and his children.
capacity_detail: Revenue almost NOK 19bn in 2024 (approx. USD 1.8bn at NOK 0.093), up from NOK 17.9bn in 2023
sponsorships: Naming-rights sponsor of Strawberry Arena (Nationalarenan), Stockholm, since January 2024
markets: Hotels in Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Finland and other Nordic markets, six markets in total
rationale: Already buys big naming rights; F1 could lift its hospitality brand among Nordic travellers but its market is regional.

name: Civica
desc: London-based software company providing management software for local government, health, education, housing and utilities.
capacity_detail: Sold by Partners Group to Blackstone for about USD 2.5bn (agreed Nov 2023, completed May 2024)
markets: Public-sector software in the UK, Australia, Singapore and North America
rationale: B2B public-sector software; F1 offers limited brand fit beyond technology positioning and employer branding.

name: Murphy Group
desc: Family-owned UK and Irish contractor delivering energy, rail, water, tunnelling and power infrastructure, founded in 1951.
capacity_detail: Turnover GBP 711m in year to December 2017 (approx. USD 924m at GBP 1.30)
markets: Infrastructure in the UK, Ireland and Canada (Surerus-Murphy joint venture)
rationale: Infrastructure contractor; Silverstone hospitality may help client relations but consumer brand value is low.
